subject: No modification indices with group comparision and ordered variables

messages.author: cd5c82a1e2e9d95e
messages.subject: No modification indices with group comparision and ordered variables
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to fit a pathmodel (no latent factors) where two variables are ordered (a 4-point scale and a dichotomous variable, alltogether there are eight variables in the model). When I fit the model sperately for my two groups (countries), eveything is fine and I am able to view the modification indices. But when I switch to group comparison, I receive an error with the modification indices:

Modification Indices:

Error in `[<-`(`*tmp*`, , x.el.idx[[mm]], value = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0,  : 
  subscript out of bounds


Further information: The model itself is estimated without an error, results are reasonable and the initial fit is ok (chi² 98, df 14, n=1600, gfi .993, rmsea 0.08).
To continue with invariance estimation I need the modification indices to see, which constraints have to be estimated freely.

I hope you have an idea and thanks for you help!


ps: Mr Russesl and colleagues: thank you for the great work! I'm so grateful that there is such an open source alternative!

On 10/16/2014 05:43 AM, Terrence Jorgensen wrote:
> There was never any syntax posted with this. I'm not sure what became

> problem, and I'm not familiar enough with the categorical CFA literature
> to know why (or in what situation) I shouldn't expect to see

In principle, you should always get modification indices.
> them for a single or multiple-group model, using this example:

> u3 ~*~ c(1, 1)*u3

I believe this one is the culprit. The modindices() function does not
know (yet) how to handle scaling factors.

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: No modification indices with group comparision and ordered variables
parts:
>     u3 ~*~ c(1, 1)*u3

I believe this one is the culprit. The modindices() function does not
know (yet) how to handle scaling factors.
I wonder if those are the only types of parameters that cause the problem.  Using this data

myData <- read.table("http://www.statmodel.com/usersguide/chap5/ex5.16.dat")
names(myData) <- c("u1","u2","u3","u4","u5","u6","x1","x2","x3","g")
myData$u1 <- ordered(myData$u1)
myData$u2 <- ordered(myData$u2)
myData$u3 <- ordered(myData$u3)
myData$u4 <- ordered(myData$u4)
myData$u5 <- ordered(myData$u5)
myData$u6 <- ordered(myData$u6)
I get the error even without the scaling parameter in the model:

model0 <- ' f1 =~ u1 + u2 + u3
f2 =~ u4 + u5 + u6
# mimic
f1 + f2 ~ x1 + x2 + x3

'
fit0 <- cfa(model0, data = myData, std.lv = TRUE)
modindices(fit0)

But when I change the regressions of latent variables onto exogenous (x1, x2, x3) into covariances, I do not get the error

model1 <- ' f1 =~ u1 + u2 + u3
f2 =~ u4 + u5 + u6

# covariances
f1 + f2 ~~ x1 + x2 + x3
'
fit1 <- cfa(model1, data = myData, std.lv = TRUE)
modindices(fit1)

I don't know if it is just the "gamma"s that cause the problem in this example.

Thanks for the help,

Terry
